title: Matching the verb: vagyok, vagy, van or megyek, mész, megy

sections.title: Two sets of verbs
sections.content: The ending and the verb go together. A place with *-ban/-ben* is used with *vagyok*, *vagy* and *van*: *A kávézóban vagyok.* A place with *-ba/-be* is used with *megyek*, *mész* and *megy*: *A kávézóba megyek.* Do not mix the sets: *A kávézóba vagyok* and *A kávézóban megyek* are both wrong.

sections.title: Being there and going there
rows: I am going to the café.
You are going to the restaurant.
Meg is going to the cinema.

items.english: Where are you? I am in the café.
Where are you going? I am going to the restaurant.

items.spanish: Meg a moziban van, Anna a moziba megy.
items.english: Meg is at the cinema, Anna is going to the cinema.

sections.content: Check two things in every sentence: the ending on the place and the verb. They must agree. A quick test: if you can ask *Hol?*, you need *-ban/-ben* and *van*; if you can ask *Hová?*, you need *-ba/-be* and *megy*.
